extracted.intended_audience: senior agency officials and legal/legislative staff (Office of General Counsel, Legislation Division) within an intelligence agency
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for deciding whether and how the agency should submit comments on OMB's draft Circular on employee parking, including what substantive arguments to make for exemptions and what procedural/political considerations to weigh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural approach options
rubrics_metrics.description: Two possible approaches toward dealing with the draft Circular: --Do nothing on the assumption that the rental value of spaces at Headquarters will be determined to be less than $10 per month and that, therefore, no fee will be charged; or — Submit comments which would, in effect, ask for an exemption for the Headquarters compound and other outlying facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh the likelihood of GSA assigning a value below the fee threshold versus the political and mission costs/benefits of actively seeking an exemption. The memo frames the decision as binary but notes it is essentially political.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair rental value / valuation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft Circular mentions the price of commercial 'property' in the vicinity; this does not necessarily mean the price of commercial parking. The Circular, moreover, says that 'the rate shall not be less than the sum of the fair rental value of such property as used in calculating Standard Level User Charges and any direct costs of parking facility management.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate how GSA will determine charges (including what 'Standard Level User Charge' means and how it's calculated). Do not assume the $10/month threshold will apply; consider that isolation or lack of commercial parking can increase fair rental value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument: uniqueness of agency mission and security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniqueness of Agency mission and security requirements: Cover considerations prevent many employees from using either public transportation or carpooling with overt employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mission- and security-related facts to argue that employees cannot reasonably use alternative transportation; cite specific operational/security constraints that make public transit or visible carpooling infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument: operational timing precludes carpooling
rubrics_metrics.description: The necessity of evening and weekend activity at our facilities precludes carpooling based on assumptions about uniform quitting times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document irregular duty hours, shift-work, or frequent off-hour requirements that make carpooling impractical for substantial numbers of employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument: isolation and lack of public transportation
rubrics_metrics.description: Isolation of the Headquarters compound: The paucity of public transport is well known. The same argument applies with regard to outlying facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of insufficient or non-existent public transit service to Headquarters and outlying facilities to support an exemption claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument: lack of available commercial parking increases lot value
rubrics_metrics.description: The lack of available commercial parking; if you drive to Headquarters you have no choice but to park in the Headquarters lot. This, it can be argued, makes the spaces in that lot more, not less, valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate local commercial parking scarcity and the 'inelastic' nature of demand for the agency's parking to counter assumptions that government parking should be priced like nearby commercial parking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative reference as supporting precedent (S.871)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two bills have been introduced on the Hill in connection with the parking issue. One of these (S.871) would exempt from charges 'parking at military bases or other isolated facilities where no nearby commercial parking exists.' We are, it seems to me, somewhat like a military base here at Headquarters and at some of our other facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant pending or enacted legislation (e.g., S.871) that provides exemptions for isolated or security-sensitive facilities as persuasive precedent or support for an exemption request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political strategy: whether to request exemption versus support policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not we have good arguments for exemption is one thing; whether we choose to use them is another. We must make an essentially political decision. Does the Agency want to put itself in the position of asking for an exemption from what is clearly a Presidential policy with respect to the rest of the Federal government? My own view is that we can support the principles behind the President's policy and take whatever steps we can to further encourage carpools, etc., while at the same time demonstrating that considerations unique to our mission and security/operational requirements should result in an exemption for the Headquarters compound and other outlying facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance public posture (supporting energy-efficiency goals) against operational needs; consider framing comments to affirm policy goals while seeking narrowly tailored exemptions grounded in mission/security facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid averaging charges across agency facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: I would, however, caution against any attempt to spread the burden by 'averaging' the cost of all Agency spaces (Headquarters and 'core') and charging accordingly. To do so could open the Agency to accusations of attempting to undermine the President's program, the purpose of which is to discourage people from driving to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid proposing or accepting cost-averaging across disparate facilities as a defense strategy; that could be perceived as undermining the President's objective and politically backfire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior approach to government-wide legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: This would be consistent with our approach to a good deal of legislation that purports to deal with issues on a government-wide basis. We are often in the position of arguing that while a proposal has merit in the abstract its application to our Agency would impact adversely on our intelligence mission or on the DCI's responsibility to protect sources and methods. We could take the same kind of approach in the parking case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage agency precedent in commenting on government-wide rules: concede general merit while explaining adverse concrete impacts on intelligence operations, sources, and methods; frame exemptions narrowly and factually.
